what: Every time the cursor moves (photo size × 150/275)px inside the area, one photo is placed — the photo is placed so the cursor sits at its upper-left .318 point, sliced into 10 horizontal strips that open sideways in .75s from the center strip outward (|i−4.5|×.1s), then 1s later close toward the center in 1s starting from the outer strips (×25ms), fading to .25. A placed photo slides to the cursor position over 1s from a lagging point (per frame 1−.9^(dt/16.7)), max 24 photos. It tracks the cursor over the whole window and draws only when inside the area box, so it continues over the header floating above the area. On touch or below 1000px, a sine path (x sin(φ+.6) · y sin(1.37φ), φ += .85/s) runs by itself (up to 12 sheets). Photos are 275 when window width is over 1000, 200 over 600, 150px below that

options.size: Image side length (px) — if omitted, 275·200·150 depending on window width
options.gap: Travel distance (px) for placing the photo, default size × 150/275
options.max: Number of photos visible at once, default 24 (12 when it loops by itself)
options.touch: If ”off”, turns off the self-rotating trail on touch and narrow screens
options.[data-fx-part=photo]: Photo to reuse (child) — hidden and copied for each strip. If absent, nothing happens

use: …
note: Does nothing under reduced motion. On touch devices it is a self-rotating trail like the original — if it should be quiet like an app, touch: off

from.where: index.js .yf-trail (Hero cursor photo trail) — original Trail: window pointermove + Hero box check, sizes 275/200/150 · threshold size×150/275 · position .318 · max 24 (auto 12), 10 strips in .75s (|i−4.5|×100ms) · out 1s (×25ms) cubic-bezier(0.87,0,0.13,1), sliding 1s cubic-bezier(.25,.46,.45,.94)
